table_title: List the world's reigning kingdoms today — sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch — with the region, type of monarchy, current monarch, and year of accession.
db_analog: SELECT country, region, type_of_monarchy, current_monarch, year_of_accession FROM sovereign_monarchies WHERE constituted_as_kingdom = TRUE AND has_own_monarch = TRUE ORDER BY country
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of current monarchies' master article + 'List of current monarchs of sovereign states' supporting article (added in cycle-1 repair to source-ground Year of Accession cells), accessed 2026-05-13. Universe is the 17 sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch — that is, states whose form of government is officially a kingdom and whose monarch is exclusively theirs (not shared with other countries via the Commonwealth realm system). The universe rule is applied as a two-clause filter on the master article's Table 1 (43-row main current-monarchies wikitable): (a) Title of Head of State contains 'King' (or 'Dragon King' for Bhutan; 'King Queen Mother' for Eswatini's dual-monarch system) — this captures the kingdom-vs-non-kingdom distinction (excludes principalities like Andorra/Liechtenstein/Monaco where the head is 'Co-Princes' or 'Prince', sultanates like Brunei/Oman, emirates like Kuwait/Qatar/UAE, the Vatican/Holy See theocracy, Luxembourg's grand duchy, Malaysia's federal elective monarchy, and Japan's emperor-led empire); AND (b) the country is NOT a Commonwealth realm of Charles III — this excludes 14 of the 15 Commonwealth realms (Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, The Bahamas, Belize, Canada, Grenada, Jamaica, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Solomon Islands, Tuvalu) which share Charles III as their head of state but are not themselves constituted as kingdoms (they are 'constitutional monarchies' or 'Commonwealth realms' but not 'Kingdoms of X'). The United Kingdom IS retained because it is the original kingdom whose monarchy the Commonwealth realms share. Per-row cells: Country is the conventional short-form English name (Belgium, not 'Kingdom of Belgium'; Denmark, not 'Kingdom of Denmark'); Region is a 6-value categorical curator-derived from standard geographic convention (Europe, Middle East, North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, Pacific); Type of Monarchy is taken verbatim from the source's Type of monarchy column (Parliamentary = 10 / Semi-constitutional = 5 / Absolute = 2); Current Monarch is taken from the per-monarchs supporting article's Monarch column (which uses the regnal short-form for most monarchs and the dual regnal-and-personal-name form 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' for Thailand specifically — the per-monarchs source's verbatim formulation); Year of Accession is the integer year the monarch assumed the throne, sourced from the per-monarchs supporting article's 'Since' column (which has full DD Month YYYY accession dates from which the year is extracted). Both the Type column and the Current Monarch / Year of Accession are dynamic: monarchs change on death/abdication (most recent: Denmark's Frederik X 2024 after Margrethe II's abdication; UK's Charles III 2022 after Elizabeth II's death). The 17-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon; new kingdoms or abolitions are rare events.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `set_filter` saturation gap (set_filter target 5; this instance brings it to 5/5, SATURATING the category — THIRD CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection and set_operation). User selected this from a 'kingdoms vs broader-monarchies' framing slate; pivot from the cycle-0 strict 'Ivy League ∩ AAU' (which was already pivoted to AAU ∩ Big Ten as the prior staged set_operation instance) — this is a separate user-driven pick for set_filter saturation. The framing 'sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch' was chosen after a deep-dive comparison of Filter A (any country with King-titled head of state, including the 15 Commonwealth realms = 31 rows) vs Filter B (kingdoms excluding Commonwealth realms = 17 rows). Filter B aligns with common-sense English usage: when an English speaker says 'the world's kingdoms', they list Spain, UK, Saudi Arabia, Thailand, etc. — they do NOT list Canada, Australia, Jamaica (which are Commonwealth realms or constitutional monarchies sharing a monarch with the UK, but not constituted as 'Kingdom of Canada'/'Kingdom of Australia'). The Wikipedia source's per-country article naming confirms this convention — articles titled 'Kingdom of Spain' / 'Kingdom of Saudi Arabia' / 'Kingdom of Sweden' exist, but NO articles titled 'Kingdom of Canada' / 'Kingdom of Australia' exist. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 2 (master 'List of current monarchies' article supplies Country and Type of Monarchy via Table 1; supporting 'List of current monarchs of sovereign states' article (added in cycle-1 repair) supplies Current Monarch and Year of Accession via its Monarch and Since columns). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse tables[1] (the 43-row main current-monarchies wikitable; tables[0] is the boilerplate-warning table), (3) filter to rows where Title of Head of State contains 'King' (31 rows), (4) further filter to exclude the 14 non-UK Commonwealth realms (those that share Charles III with UK), yielding 17 rows, (5) for each, take Country name in conventional English short-form (the master table's Monarchy column uses 'Kingdom of Denmark' / 'Kingdom of the Netherlands' but the staged Country cell uses 'Denmark' / 'Netherlands' per common-name convention), Type of Monarchy verbatim from the master article's Type column, Current Monarch verbatim from the supporting per-monarchs article's Monarch column (uses 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' for Thailand specifically — the per-monarchs source's verbatim dual regnal-and-personal-name form), Year of Accession as the integer year extracted from the supporting per-monarchs article's Since column (full 'DD Month YYYY' accession dates from which the year is taken). Result: 17 rows × 5 columns, PK on Country, 0 duplicates. Region distribution: Europe 7 (UK, Spain, Belgium, Denmark, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden), Middle East 3 (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Bahrain), Asia 3 (Thailand, Cambodia, Bhutan), Sub-Saharan Africa 2 (Lesotho, Eswatini), North Africa 1 (Morocco), Pacific 1 (Tonga). Type distribution: Parliamentary 10, Semi-constitutional 5, Absolute 2 (Saudi Arabia, Eswatini). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical European kingdoms (UK Charles III 2022, Spain Felipe VI 2014, Sweden Carl XVI Gustaf 1973) and the major non-European kingdoms (Saudi Arabia Salman 2015, Jordan Abdullah II 1999, Thailand Rama X (Vajiralongkorn) 2016); harder calibration cells include the smaller / less-headline-grabbing kingdoms (Lesotho Letsie III 1996, Eswatini Mswati III 1986, Bhutan Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck 2006, Tonga Tupou VI 2012); the most-recent succession events (Denmark Frederik X January 2024; UK Charles III September 2022) test up-to-date knowledge; the cell-type ambiguities — Bahrain became a Kingdom in 2002 (was an emirate before), Cambodia's monarchy was restored in 1993, Eswatini renamed from Swaziland in 2018 — test deeper knowledge of recent constitutional changes.
